newsitem.title: UK: Southern Co to bid for Bewag - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Southern Co to bid for Bewag - WSJ.

text.p: Southern Co of the United States has joined the bidding for German state utility group Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag), in which several German and foreign firms have already shown interest, the Wall Street Journal Europe reported on Thursday.
Government officials voted in favour of Bewag's full privatisation last week, clearing a major hurdle for the company's sale. The decision must now be approved by parliament.
The Wall Street Journal said Southern Co was believed to be the only U.S. bidder for the German utility.
"I can confirm we are looking," the paper quoted a Southern spokesman as saying.

The paper said other U.S. firms, including General Electric Co, had complained that the German utility sector was closed to outsiders. It added this sale would be a major test of whether Germany has opened its utility market to foreigners.
The state currently owns 50.8 percent of Bewag and has been negotiating since last year to sell a 25.8 percent package.
Utilities Bayernwerk, a unit of Viag AG, and Preussenelektra, owned by Veba AG, each hold a further 10 percent in the company and the remainder is held by smaller shareholders.
Viag AG has confirmed it is interested in increasing the stake and industry sources said last December that it planned to make a joint bid with Veba for a higher stake.
